findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the user_data script, exposing long-term credentials to anyone with access to the instance metadata, console, or Terraform state.
Ingress rule allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance's administrative interface to the entire internet.
Ingress rule allows HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While this may be intentional for a public web server, combined with no HTTPS/TLS this exposes traffic to interception and unrestricted access.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to all instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on the volume is not encrypted.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs does not configure server-side encryption, leaving potentially sensitive network traffic metadata stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined to restrict public access, and force_destroy is enabled, risking unintended public exposure or data loss of flow log archives.

findings.issue_category: no encryption in transit for web traffic
findings.description: The instance serves content over plain HTTP (apache2) with no TLS configuration, allowing sensitive data to be transmitted unencrypted.
